prompt: Ana saves $\$4$ every week and Ben saves $\$6$ every week. Both start at $\$0$. After $5$ weeks, how many more dollars does Ben have than Ana?
hint: Each person's savings make a pattern that grows by the same amount every week. Compare the two patterns at the same week.

hints.text: Each person's savings make a pattern that grows by the same amount every week. Compare the two patterns at the same week.
After $5$ weeks Ana has $5 \times 4$ dollars and Ben has $5 \times 6$ dollars. Find both amounts and then subtract.
Ana has $\$20$ and Ben has $\$30$, and $30 - 20 = 10$, so Ben has $\$10$ more than Ana.

explanation: Ana's pattern is $4, 8, 12, 16, 20$, so after $5$ weeks she has $5 \times 4 = \$20$.
Ben's pattern is $6, 12, 18, 24, 30$, so after $5$ weeks he has $5 \times 6 = \$30$.
$30 - 20 = 10$, so Ben has $\$10$ more than Ana.
